title: Per-record encrypted analytic slices with redaction-at-ingest and verifiable deletion receipts
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Our current analytics materialized aggregates and event stores require large-scale rewrites to prove erasure when customers request deletion or when consent toggles. Backfills are expensive and leave audit gaps. We need a pattern that allows (1) immediate redaction/erasure of identifiable data without reprocessing weeks of derived datasets, and (2) produces a verifiable deletion receipt for compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: Implement per-record envelope encryption for incoming analytics events where the event body (PII fields) is stored encrypted with an ephemeral data key tied to a deletion token.

Provide an API to issue a deletion token revocation which causes those encrypted blobs to become unrecoverable (provable deletion) without touching derived aggregates metadata or running heavy backfills.
Console UI + audit export shows deletion receipts (token id, scope, timestamp) that map to the number of encrypted blobs and shards affected; this data can be exported for legal requests.
End-to-end latency impact for ingest path stays under +20ms p50; storage cost delta <10% for first year; no regression on existing SLOs for console analytics ingestion.
Automated integration test that simulates a deletion request and proves docs are unreadable via KMS key checks and that downstream dashboards show redaction markers rather than raw PII.
implementation_notes: Design: wrap PII fields in an 'ephemeral_envelope' encrypted with a DEK (data encryption key). DEKs are encrypted with a rotating master KMS key and indexed by a deletion_token id.

Ingest: transformer lambda (ingest-transform) will detect PII schema, generate DEK, encrypt PII fields, and emit event with deletion_token reference + encrypted_blob. Non-PII remains plaintext for analytics.
Storage: data written to long-term events S3/Parquet with an extra column deletion_token and envelope_metadata. Use compacted partitioning by customer_id/date to allow efficient token accounting.

Deletion: revoking a deletion_token triggers two actions: (A) orchestrator records deletion_receipt and marks token revoked; (B) KMS rotate/expire path destroys DEKs or deletes KMS-wrapped keys to make blobs unrecoverable.
Audit: console export will surface deletion_receipt JSON with token id, scope (customer, project, date-range), counts by partition, and KMS action id for attestation.
migration_plan: Phase 0 (spike): instrument small subset of ingestion (5% traffic) with envelope format and measure p50/p95 latency and storage overhead.
Phase 1 (opt-in customers): enable per-customer flag to write encrypted envelopes while keeping existing views unchanged. No backfills performed in this phase.
Phase 2 (hybrid): downstream consumers are updated to respect 'redaction_marker' for encrypted fields. Start serving redaction-aware dashboards for opt-in customers.

Phase 3 (opt-out/backfill): provide scheduled backfill tool that can reingest historical data through ingest-transform to convert old events into envelopes for customers that require full provable-history (costly, opt-in).
dependencies: Security/KMS team - permissions and destruction workflow (ticket TBD)
Console frontend - audit export UI and deletion receipt display (PM/Design work)
Observability - tracing hooks to link deletion_token -> S3 objects and metrics
comments: 2025-11-10 Aisha Kumar: Created ticket after privacy sync — this is intended to reduce backfill costs and provide a clean legal deletion primitive.
2025-11-12 Marco Diaz: Spike started; implemented basic envelope encrypt/decrypt using local KMS emulator. Observed +12ms p50 on transform; p95 +28ms due to crypto GC.
2025-11-14 Security review: noted requirement to ensure deletion_token revocation includes auditable KMS operation id. Also flagged risk if DEKs are replicated outside of S3 (caches).

2025-11-15 Eng/Tier-Infra: identified blocker — current streaming buffer (streamer-v2) flattens columns and we'd have to add envelope metadata without breaking consumers. Added dependency on ENG-582901.
2025-11-18 Marco Diaz: Next actions — prototype KMS-wrapped DEK storage schema, add deletion token indexing table (compact), and coordinate with console UX for deletion_receipt shape.
